h1: Hop Inn Bangkok Onnut Station — the cheapest clean hotel right by BTS On Nut
intro: If you need just two things — a clean room and a short walk to the BTS — Hop Inn Bangkok Onnut Station is the most direct answer on outer Sukhumvit. It is a 2-star budget chain hotel with 133 rooms, opened in 2022, on Sukhumvit Soi 52. The walk from the lobby to BTS On Nut is roughly 260 metres, about 3 minutes. Every room comes with a private balcony, fridge, air conditioning, free Wi-Fi, and there is free on-site parking. Rates start from approx. THB 700–900/night, with a score of 8.8 from 957 Booking.com reviews — an unusually strong result for a hotel in this price bracket. Two things to know up front: Hop Inn does not offer day-use or hourly rates (overnight bookings only, check-in 14:00 / check-out 12:00), and this is On Nut, outer Sukhumvit — not the Asok or Nana core. But if those details suit your trip, this is the best-value clean bed in the neighbourhood by some distance.

body.html: Hop Inn is a Thai budget-hotel chain that has expanded across the country, and the On Nut branch, opened in 2022, is one of its better-performing Bangkok outposts. The headline number — 8.8 out of 10 from nearly a thousand Booking.com reviews — reflects a simple formula that works: a clean room close to the BTS at a price most competitors struggle to match. Guests returning from reviews across platforms repeat the same points — fast walk to the station, reliably cool air conditioning, and rooms that are tidier than the price implies.

The room range is straightforward. Standard Double rooms (one larger bed) and Standard Twin rooms (two single beds) come in at around 17.6 sq m — small but efficiently laid out, with nothing wasted. Every room has a private balcony, refrigerator, air conditioning, flat-screen TV, and free Wi-Fi. The hotel opened recently enough (2022) that everything is in good condition — there are no complaints about worn-out fittings or dated bathrooms that surface so often in older budget properties. A HOP Plus Room upgrade is also available for guests who want a little more space.
"Small room but incredibly clean. The AC was powerful — slept brilliantly. Free parking right in the hotel and BTS On Nut is a two-minute stroll. For the price, nothing comes close."

The immediate neighbourhood around Sukhumvit Soi 52 is On Nut, on the outer end of the Sukhumvit BTS line. That is worth stating plainly — this is not Asok, Nana or Thong Lo. What it is: a genuinely liveable Bangkok neighbourhood with Lotus's On Nut within a 7-minute walk, Habito Mall nearby, a cluster of local restaurants and food stalls, and multiple 7-Elevens virtually on the doorstep. The BTS from On Nut connects you to Ekkamai and Thong Lo in two stops, Terminal 21 Asok in three or four, and the Airport Rail Link interchange at Makkasan (via BTS Phaya Thai) for Suvarnabhumi Airport in around 30 minutes.

The consistent criticism in guest reviews comes down to amenities that are simply absent. There is no shampoo, toothbrush, toothpaste or hairdryer in the room. There is no kettle, tea or coffee in the room either (the hotel does provide complimentary coffee and hot chocolate from a lobby station in the morning). There is no in-room safe, which concerns some guests travelling with valuables or passports. A few reviews mention noise carrying between rooms or floors, and the occasional guest notes that while staff are friendly enough, they do not proactively follow up on issues — you need to raise problems yourself. None of these are dealbreakers for the price point, but they are worth knowing.

The one thing that is important to say directly: Hop Inn Bangkok Onnut operates on standard overnight check-in only — there are no day-use, day-rate or hourly booking options. This is a 24-hour check-in policy, but the minimum stay is a full night. If you need a room for a few hours during the day, look elsewhere. If you want the cheapest clean overnight base right next to the BTS on outer Sukhumvit, with free parking included, this is the right place.

highlights.title: 3-minute walk to BTS On Nut
highlights.text: Around 260 metres from the hotel entrance to BTS On Nut station — straightforward walk, no main roads to cross. Direct line to central Sukhumvit and the Airport Rail Link interchange.

highlights.title: Cheapest clean hotel in the area
highlights.text: Rates from approx. THB 700–900/night — lower than any equivalent clean hotel on outer Sukhumvit. Free Wi-Fi and free parking included at no extra charge.

highlights.text: Opened in 2022, so fittings are still in good order. Reviewers repeatedly note that rooms are cleaner and better maintained than they expected for the rate. Strong air conditioning praised across reviews.

honestSummary: Hop Inn Onnut does one thing very well: it gives you a clean, private room with a BTS-adjacent location for around THB 700. It does not pretend to be anything else. The amenities are minimal by design — no toiletries, no kettle, no pool — and there are no day-use rates. Within those limits, the value is hard to fault for the price.
honestChecks: If you expect a full amenities kit — there is no shampoo, toothbrush, toothpaste or hairdryer in rooms → bring your own or grab what you need from the 7-Eleven next door
If you want a day-use room or hourly rate — Hop Inn has no day-use option, overnight only → try Citrus Sukhumvit 13, which offers bookable day-use slots online
If central Sukhumvit (Asok, Nana) matters for your trip — On Nut is 3–4 BTS stops further out → if location in the core beats price, budget hotels closer to Asok may suit you better

tips.title: Walking to BTS On Nut
tips.body: Turn left out of the hotel, walk along Sukhumvit Soi 52 to the main Sukhumvit Road, then follow the signs up to BTS On Nut station. The whole walk takes about 3 minutes at a comfortable pace.

tips.title: Shopping and food nearby
tips.body: Lotus's On Nut supermarket is within a 7-minute walk for groceries and meals. Multiple 7-Elevens are essentially on the doorstep. Habito Mall is also close for restaurants and coffee shops.

tips.title: Bring your own toiletries
tips.body: Hop Inn does not supply shampoo, toothbrush, toothpaste or a hairdryer. Pack them or buy very cheaply at the nearby 7-Eleven or Lotus's before you check in.

tips.title: Getting to the airports
tips.body: BTS On Nut connects to the Airport Rail Link interchange at Phaya Thai (about 8 stops). Total journey to Suvarnabhumi Airport is around 30–35 minutes. A taxi from the hotel runs approx. THB 250–350 and takes 30–45 minutes depending on traffic.

faqTitle: FAQ — Hop Inn Bangkok Onnut Station

faq.q: How far is Hop Inn Bangkok Onnut Station from the BTS?
faq.a: The hotel is on Sukhumvit Soi 52, approximately 260 metres — about a 3-minute walk — from BTS On Nut station. There is no main road to cross; it is a straightforward walk along the soi to the station.

faq.q: Does Hop Inn Bangkok Onnut offer day-use or hourly rates?
faq.a: No. Hop Inn operates on overnight bookings only (check-in 14:00, check-out 12:00). There are no day-use packages or hourly rates. If you need a room for daytime use only, Citrus Sukhumvit 13 offers bookable day-use slots online.

faq.q: What is the price range at Hop Inn Bangkok Onnut?
faq.a: Standard rooms start from approximately THB 700–900 per night, depending on the season and availability. This makes it one of the most affordable clean hotels on outer Sukhumvit.

faq.q: Is free parking available at Hop Inn Bangkok Onnut?
faq.a: Yes — the hotel has free on-site parking, which is a significant advantage in Bangkok, where many hotels charge separately for this.

faq.q: What area is Hop Inn Bangkok Onnut in, and what is nearby?
faq.a: The hotel sits in the On Nut neighbourhood on outer Sukhumvit — not the busy core of Asok or Nana, but a practical local area with Lotus's On Nut supermarket, Habito Mall, a number of local restaurants, and multiple 7-Elevens all within easy walking distance.
